evals.prompt: How many parameters does attention account for in GPT-3, and how is that number built up?
evals.expected_output: Key and query matrices are 128 x 12,288 (~1.5M each); value down/up make four equal matrices, ~6.3M per head; 96 heads give ~600M per block; 96 layers give just under 58B, about a third of the 175B total.
expectations: States ~6.3M parameters per head (02 3Blue1Brown, Counting parameters ~1101s)
States ~600M per multi-head block with 96 heads (02 3Blue1Brown, Multiple heads ~1316s)
States just under 58B in total, about a third of 175B (02 3Blue1Brown, Going deeper ~1461s)

evals.prompt: In the original Transformer, what are d_model, the number of heads and d_k, and what number do the scores get divided by?
evals.expected_output: d_model = 512, h = 8, d_k = d_v = 64; scores are divided by sqrt(d_k) = 8.
expectations: States d_model = 512, h = 8, d_k = 64 (01 paper, 3.2.2 / 03 Illustrated, Self-Attention in Detail)
States scores are divided by 8 = sqrt(64) (03 Illustrated, Self-Attention in Detail or 01 paper 3.2.1)

evals.prompt: How do you mask future tokens in attention, and why not just set those scores to zero? Is masking used in cross-attention?
evals.expected_output: Set the masked entries to negative infinity before the softmax so they become 0 afterwards while columns stay normalized; setting them to zero directly would break normalization. Cross-attention typically has no masking since there is no notion of later tokens affecting earlier ones.
expectations: Says set entries to -infinity before softmax (02 3Blue1Brown Masking ~731s, or 01 paper 3.2.3 / 03 Illustrated Decoder Side)
Explains that zeroing directly would break normalization (02 3Blue1Brown, Masking ~731s)
Says cross-attention typically uses no masking (02 3Blue1Brown, Cross-attention ~1132s)

evals.prompt: I need my model to handle sentences longer than any seen in training. Which positional encoding should I pick, and how much does the choice cost in quality?
evals.expected_output: Sinusoidal: the paper chose it because it may extrapolate to longer sequences, and the Illustrated Transformer also notes it scales to unseen lengths; learned positional embeddings gave nearly identical results (Table 3 row E). (The Illustrated Transformer's figure concatenates sine/cosine halves from Tensor2Tensor; the paper interleaves them.)
expectations: Recommends sinusoidal encodings for extrapolation to unseen lengths (01 paper 3.5 or 03 Illustrated, Positional Encoding)
Says learned embeddings gave nearly identical results (01 paper, Table 3 row E)

evals.prompt: 3Blue1Brown applies softmax down columns of the attention pattern; the paper writes softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V. Do they disagree?
evals.expected_output: No, it is a layout difference: 3Blue1Brown puts keys on rows and queries on columns and normalizes each column; in the paper Q has one query per row, so softmax runs along each row of QK^T. Same operation, transposed grid.
expectations: Says 3Blue1Brown normalizes each column so it sums to 1 (02 3Blue1Brown, The attention pattern ~589s)
Says the difference is notation/layout (transposed grid, queries as rows in the paper), not a different computation (01 paper eq. 1 vs 02 video)
